finding.claim: After readBlock() fails validation or checksum (IOException), the stream does not reset its read state. originalLen is committed from the attacker-supplied header before the block is verified, and o is not reset on failure. A caller that catches the IOException and calls read() again receives plaintext from the unverified block (e.g. buffer[0] on the first block).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes in the compressed input stream: the 13-byte block header (originalLen at MAGIC_LENGTH+5) and the block payload, which is decompressed into buffer.
finding.sink: read() (line 204 buffer[o++]) and read(byte[],int,int) (lines 219-220 System.arraycopy) return unauthenticated plaintext to the application after the checksum has failed.

trace.note: First read(): o == originalLen (0 == 0), so refill() -> readBlock().
originalLen = readIntLE(header) is assigned from attacker-controlled header data before any validation.
buffer grown to originalLen if needed.
safeDecompressor.decompress(...) writes plaintext into buffer[0..originalLen) (322 on the fast-decompressor path).
checksum.getValue() != check -> throw new IOException("Stream is corrupted") at 336-338. o is still 0 and originalLen is now the attacker's value N; o = 0 at line 339 is never reached.
o (0) != originalLen (N), so refill() is skipped.
Returns buffer[0] & 0xFF, plaintext from the block that failed its checksum. available() (line 190) also reports N - o as if the data were valid.

finding.guards_checked: Header magic check (262-272), compression-method check (276), originalLen/compressedLen range and RAW/LZ4 consistency checks (283-291), the LZ4 acceptOversizedBlocks gate (289), decompressor length check (318/323), XXHash32 content checksum (334-338). All of these run after originalLen is assigned, and none of them invalidates the stream state on failure. Contrast: LZ4FrameInputStream.java:313 and :356-357 keep buffer.limit(0) until the block is verified, and only then expose the data. Mitigating factor: exposure requires the application to catch IOException and keep reading the same stream; a normal propagate-and-stop caller is not affected.
finding.repro: Build a valid LZ4BlockOutputStream stream whose first block contains known plaintext (e.g. 'secret...'), then corrupt the 4-byte XXHash32 check field in that block's header (offset 9 from the start of the header). Then: LZ4BlockInputStream in = LZ4BlockInputStream.newBuilder().build(bytes); try { in.read(); } catch (IOException e) { /* ignored */ } ; int b = in.read(); // returns 's' (0x73) from the failed block instead of -1 or an exception. Not executed: derived from code reading only.
